scene_text: INT. HOTEL CORRIDOR SET - NIGHT. A long corridor flat built on stage, 8 metres wide and 4 deep, with three doors along the back wall. LEO (12) walks slowly left to right along the corridor, trailing his fingers on the wall. At the third door he stops: two figures in identical dresses stand at the far end, by the right wall. He freezes. The camera should follow him low and steady from behind his shoulder, then hold as the figures are revealed.

scene.title: Itsy Bitsy Corridor
scene.logline: A boy trailing his fingers along a hotel corridor wall stops at the third door and finds two identical figures waiting at the far end.

beats.description: Leo enters frame left, trailing fingers along the corridor wall, camera low and steady behind his shoulder.
Leo passes the second door; his fingers keep brushing the wall, footsteps echoing.
Leo reaches the third door and stops; camera holds as the two identical figures are revealed at the far end by the right wall.
Leo freezes; the figures stand perfectly still, heads slightly tilted, staring back.
Both figures step forward in perfect unison; the camera jolts as they lunge toward Leo.

references.moment: Steadicam tracks low behind Danny's tricycle down the Overlook corridor.
references.why: Directly serves t=0s — the camera sits low and steady behind a small figure moving down a corridor, and the analysis notes the tracking "gives a feeling of him being followed by something unknown."

references.moment: Opening 360° pan follows Annie fleeing, never showing what chases her.
references.technique: Continuous 360° panning shot; threat kept in off-screen space.
references.why: Serves t=4s–t=8s — the relentless panning builds creeping dread and teaches the audience that danger arrives "from where you aren't looking," exactly the corridor-reveal logic of the third door.

references.moment: Lorraine's 18-second walk down the hallway to the door; Valak appears over her shoulder.
references.technique: Long hallway tracking shot cut against POV; handheld jolt.
references.why: Serves t=8s–t=12s — the analysis times the walk at 18 seconds of held tension before the reveal, then the handheld shake delivers the jolt when the figure finally moves.

references.moment: Night-vision camera pan reveals a crawler standing silently among the group.
references.technique: Slow POV pan into darkness; reveal with no musical sting.
references.why: Serves t=10s–t=12s — the article notes the scare "comes with no warning and no loud noise," the perfect model for two figures standing perfectly still before the unison lunge.

techniques.name: Peek around the corner
techniques.effect: the camera itself behaves like an intruder
techniques.move: Camera starts hidden behind a wall or doorframe and slowly leans out to reveal the room.
techniques.rig_notes: Small lateral move plus a slight yaw. Do not intersect the wall prop.
techniques.matched_beat: Leo enters frame left, trailing fingers along the corridor wall, camera low and steady behind his shoulder. (creeping dread then jolt)

techniques.name: Mirror reveal
techniques.effect: the jump scare is behind the character, seen in a reflection
techniques.move: Frame the character in a mirror; push gently or rack focus as a figure appears behind them.
techniques.rig_notes: Keep the camera out of the mirror's reflection line: angle 20-30 degrees off the mirror normal.
techniques.matched_beat: Leo reaches the third door and stops; camera holds as the two identical figures are revealed at the far end by the right wall. (creeping dread then jolt)

techniques.name: Slow tilt-up from feet
techniques.effect: dread of what the face will look like
techniques.move: Start framing feet or floor, tilt up slowly to the figure's face; camera height constant.
techniques.rig_notes: Pure tilt is wrist work; keep the camera at least 1.2 m from the figure.
techniques.matched_beat: Leo enters frame left, trailing fingers along the corridor wall, camera low and steady behind his shoulder. (creeping dread then jolt)

techniques.name: Slow lateral reveal
techniques.effect: suspense; the audience scans the frame for what is hidden
techniques.move: Track sideways past a doorway, pillar or furniture so a figure is revealed in the background.
techniques.rig_notes: The ideal rail move: mostly the carriage axis, joints almost static.
techniques.examples: Hereditary attic; The Conjuring clapping game
techniques.matched_beat: Leo enters frame left, trailing fingers along the corridor wall, camera low and steady behind his shoulder. (creeping dread then jolt)

techniques.name: Low-angle menace
techniques.effect: the threat towers over the viewer
techniques.move: Camera at 0.3-0.6 m height tilted up at the antagonist, slight slow push.
techniques.rig_notes: Keep the camera above 0.3 m; the arm needs room under the elbow.
techniques.examples: Nosferatu shadow on the stairs; The Babadook
techniques.matched_beat: Leo enters frame left, trailing fingers along the corridor wall, camera low and steady behind his shoulder. (creeping dread then jolt)

techniques.name: Creeping push-in
techniques.effect: slow-building dread; the audience feels drawn toward something they do not want to see
techniques.move: Dolly straight toward the subject at 5-15 cm/s, eye level or slightly below, lens fixed.
techniques.rig_notes: Easy for the rail; keep it on one axis so joint speeds stay tiny.
techniques.examples: Jaws beach push-ins; Hereditary dinner table
techniques.matched_beat: Both figures step forward in perfect unison; the camera jolts as they lunge toward Leo. (creeping dread then jolt)

shot_list.director_notes: Only S4 was rejected: the elbow was asked to accelerate 1.4x past limit during the 0.70 s move from the held frame to the reveal. I kept S1, S2 and S3 exactly as approved — the low behind-the-boy push-in, the locked-look_at lateral drift at ~0.15 m/s, and the parked pure tilt — and rebuilt S4's timing only: the move now takes 1.0 s instead of 0.7 s (every later keyframe shifted by 0.30 s), so the elbow sweeps the same 3-degree yaw and the same carriage step of 0.2 m but with 43% more time, putting every axis back under limit. The scare still lands on the move: the audience sits on Leo's frozen face for a full second, then the carriage jolts and the two figures snap into frame mid-step.

shots.name: Behind the Boy
shots.intent: Put the audience at a child's height behind Leo so the empty corridor ahead feels like it is waiting for him.
shots.reference_title: The Shining (1980) — Steadicam tracks low behind Danny's tricycle down the Overlook corridor

shots.name: The Long Walk
shots.intent: A relentless sideways drift that keeps the far end of the corridor just out of frame, teaching the audience the danger is always where they are not looking.
shots.reference_title: It Follows (2014) — Opening 360° pan follows Annie fleeing, never showing what chases her

shots.name: Third Door
shots.intent: Hold Leo small and low while the two figures resolve at the far end, so the reveal arrives with no music and no cut, only a slow tilt up.
shots.reference_title: The Descent (2005) — Night-vision camera pan reveals a crawler standing silently among the group

shots.name: The Lunge
shots.intent: A hard carriage jolt that snaps the audience from Leo's frozen face to the two figures mid-step, so the scare lands on the move itself.
shots.reference_title: The Conjuring 2 (2016) — Lorraine's 18-second walk down the hallway to the door; Valak appears over her shoulder

shot_list.director_notes: We shoot the corridor as a single unbroken geography: the rail lives at y=2.9, running x=0.6 to 4.6, so the arm always works from the open fourth wall side and never crosses an actor or a door prop. Shots 1-3 are slow, patient rail moves that keep the threat in off-screen space; shot 4 is the only fast move in the film, a 0.3 s whip-pan jolt that lands on the figures the instant they step. Every camera position stays at least 0.8 m from Leo's marks and the figure marks, and the arm never reaches over an actor to get anywhere.

shot_list.director_notes: I moved the rail to y=2.9 spanning x=0.6..4.6 so the arm always works from the open fourth wall and never crosses an actor or door prop, and I rebuilt every move so the camera stays within 1.0 m of the rail line and 0.3-1.9 m high. The big fixes: S2's lateral reveal was sweeping too much angle too fast, so I cut it to a near-pure carriage slide with the look_at held on a fixed far point (joints almost static, rail speed under 1.5 m/s); S3's tilt-up was a wrist snap, so I stretched it to a slow 6 s tilt with the camera parked and only the look_at rising; S4's whip-pan was physically impossible, so I replaced it with a fast-but-legal carriage jolt plus a small yaw that eases in over 0.25 s before the snap, keeping the scare on the move itself. Every keyframe is now reachable from the rail line and every axis stays under its speed and acceleration limit.

shot_list.director_notes: I kept the rail at y=2.9 (x=0.6..4.6) and the low behind-the-boy push-in exactly as approved, then rebuilt the two rejected moves around the physics. S2's lateral reveal was sweeping the look_at across the corridor while the carriage accelerated, which blew up wrist 1 and the rail; I locked the look_at to a single fixed far point (x=5.0) and cut the carriage travel to 0.6 m over 4 s, so the joints are essentially static and the rail never exceeds ~0.15 m/s. S4's jolt was a 0.25 s snap that demanded 6x rail acceleration and 291 deg/s on the elbow; I stretched the ease to 0.7 s, halved the carriage step to 0.2 m, and cut the yaw from 6 to 3 degrees, so the scare still lands on the move but every axis stays under limit. S3 is unchanged: camera parked, pure slow tilt, 6 s.

notes: Listen up. The scare is the third door: two identical figures waiting at the far end, and we never cut to them — the camera finds them. S1 puts us at Leo's shoulder, low and creeping. S2 drifts sideways, keeping the far end out of frame so the audience leans in. S3 tilts up slow, no music, no cut — let the silence do the work. S4 is the jolt: snap from Leo's face to them mid-step. Three rig revisions before we roll. Safety: the dolly track runs tight to the wall — keep fingers and cables clear of the wheels.
